records.original_sql: SELECT c, a, a FROM ex.data.cache_multicol WHERE a = 3;
records.replacement_sql: SELECT c, a, a AS a_duplicate FROM ex.data.cache_multicol WHERE a = 3;
records.reason: DataFusion requires unique projection names; aliasing the duplicate expression changes only its column label, not its value or cache projection.

records.original_sql: SELECT SUM(c), SUM(a), SUM(a) FROM (SELECT c, a, a AS a2 FROM ex.data.cache_multicol) t(c, a, a2);
records.replacement_sql: SELECT SUM(c), SUM(a), SUM(a) AS a_duplicate FROM (SELECT c, a, a AS a2 FROM ex.data.cache_multicol) t(c, a, a2);
records.reason: DataFusion requires unique aggregate output names; the alias preserves the duplicated aggregate value asserted by SQLLogicTest.

records.original_sql: SELECT LIST(n) FROM (SELECT n FROM ex.data.cache_big ORDER BY n LIMIT 3 OFFSET 2500);
records.replacement_sql: SELECT array_agg(n ORDER BY n) FROM (SELECT n FROM ex.data.cache_big ORDER BY n LIMIT 3 OFFSET 2500);
records.reason: DataFusion's array_agg is the equivalent list aggregate; explicit ordering preserves the replay window exactly.
